title: Would you support someone who use AI to steal from other small indie dev?
author: Ashamed-Cost-5548
selftext: If someone uses AI to copy a demo (gameplay, artstyle, hook, basically the essence) made by an indie dev who does not use AI and  publish it before the said indie dev could release it, would this sub celebrate it or be against it?

comments.author: Slow-Win8148
comments.body: Hell no, use AI to accelerate YOUR idea into existence not steal someone else.

replies.author: Ashamed-Cost-5548
replies.body: lots of indie dev are actually hesitant to share their demo or even market their game rn

replies.author: Ashamed-Cost-5548
replies.body: in case of gen art, lots of people harras atrist who express their discomfort when their art is fed to AI tho. some even go as far as feeding the art themself hust to piss the artist

comments.author: BusinessZestyclose86
comments.body: Against it obviously. If someone likes a game that much they should ask the dev if they can make a spin off. If they say no, respect it.

replies.author: Ashamed-Cost-5548
replies.body: that is not what is happening in gen art tho. lots of people steal anyway. lots of indie dev are even afraid to share their update or demo rn because bad actor can copy it and bastardize it while the original need few more months

replies.author: BusinessZestyclose86
replies.body: This kind of thing happens all the time. The only thing you can do is try to get it taken down and/or publicly shame them.

replies.author: Ashamed-Cost-5548
replies.body: spin off is out of question, the game is not finished. also there is always bad actor. I guess my question is what would the community's attitude about it

replies.author: BusinessZestyclose86
replies.body: Not really, it depends on the dev. If someone asked me, I would tell them to go for it as it would really be two different games. And if it’s a project I’ve been working months on, them producing something in a few days will be a shittier version anyway most likely.  You can’t help that there are bad actors who will do it anyway in any community.

comments.author: erofamiliar
comments.body: Completely against it, it's dogshit behavior.

replies.author: Ashamed-Cost-5548
replies.body: i know that would be the answer, but what would the community do if there is bad actor?

comments.author: No-Marionberry-772
comments.body:
its obviously not okay to steal, and intentionally trying to undercut them is a dick move. 

However, what they take wont be the same as what is being made unless it was released already and they bought and thoroughly played it.  

So its kind of weird you know?

replies.author: Ashamed-Cost-5548
replies.body:
it is a dick move. and yes it would be different output. But it will be demoralizing nonetheless and in some way worse because it is basically bastardizing someone else vision.

I guess my real question is what would this community do about it?

there should be more discussion around it

comments.author: ponderdiggums
comments.body: Of course not. AI or not, rip offs are lame.

comments.author: redditscraperbot2
comments.body:
Would you be okay with \[objectionably bad behavior\]?

Of course not. I’m more curious what the motivation behind the question is.

replies.author: Ashamed-Cost-5548
replies.body:
bad actor exist. what would the community do about it? 

also in gen art, people happily harass artist who don't want to use AI or express their discomfort when their art is stolen.

comments.author: One_Salty_Pigeon
comments.body:
I think it goes with out saying that most everyone in this group is against someone using AI to steal other peoples video game ideas. That being said I keep seeing you talk about people being afraid to post there game etc.... it's been this way before AI was a thing to the processes are just accelerated now. I mean god look at how many supermarket sim rip offs exist that add NOTHING to the genre.

For every popular game you'll get 10 lower quality copies right by it side. It's been that way before AI and it will continue to be that way moving forward.

Beyond that making a good well thought out game takes time. So the shitty copy paste versions of an actually good game tend to flop and go no where. So unless your game idea is so simple and easy to copy it only takes a few prompts (which then is it really even that good of a game) most people shouldn't be afraid of there game ideas being stolen.

replies.author: Ashamed-Cost-5548
replies.body:
except that before AI, it takes months to copy a game. the risk is higher.

the sheer speed and volume is the problem.

Thomas Brush also discussed about it. Saying all indie dev may need to restructure how their game should be marketed and launched, whwn to release demo and that kickstarter may not be tricky at this point
